title: Sliced infinity-cosmoi: one named lemma per nontrivial component of the cosmos structure
intent: State that the isofibrations over a fixed base B form an infinity-cosmos K_{/B} by listing its seven defining items, then prove it by a survey that verifies each item in turn and hands the three nontrivial verifications (pullback stability of equivalences, and its converse) to three named lemmas stated earlier in the same blueprint.

parent.name: prop:sliced-cosmoi
parent.statement: For any infinity-cosmos K and any infinity-category B in K there is an infinity-cosmos K_{/B} of isofibrations over B, whose objects are isofibrations p : E -> B with codomain B; whose functor spaces, isofibrations, terminal object and products, pullbacks and towers, and cotensors are each constructed by pullback in K (or created by the forgetful functor K_{/B} -> K); and in which a map over B is an equivalence in K_{/B} if and only if it is an equivalence in K.
parent.note: Blueprint proposition node (label prop:sliced-cosmoi). The proposition states the seven items of the structure; its proof (lines 881-901) is the glue that verifies each item in turn.

children.name: lem:trivial-fib-conical
children.statement: The trivial fibrations in an infinity-cosmos define a subcategory containing the isomorphisms and are stable under product, pullback, and forming inverse limits of towers.
children.closed_by: its own proof (content.tex:425-427), which reduces the stability to the corresponding stability of trivial fibrations of quasi-categories, a class defined by a right lifting property
children.note: Blueprint lemma node; \uses{defn:cosmos, defn:trivial-fibration}. Paired with lem:brown-fact by the glue's footnote (line 891) for the pullback-stability of equivalences.

children.name: lem:brown-fact
children.statement: Any functor f : A -> B in an infinity-cosmos may be factored as an equivalence followed by an isofibration, where this equivalence is constructed as a section of a trivial fibration. Moreover, f is an equivalence if and only if the isofibration p is a trivial fibration.
children.closed_by: its own proof (content.tex:558-567), which constructs Pf by a pullback of an isofibration and uses the 2-of-3 property (lem:equivalence-2-of-3) for the iff
children.note: Blueprint lemma node; \uses{defn:cosmos, defn:equivalence, defn:trivial-fibration}. The second lemma in the pullback-stability footnote (line 891).

children.name: lem:equiv-htpy-equiv
children.statement: A map f : A -> B between infinity-categories in an infinity-cosmos K is an equivalence if and only if it extends to the data of a homotopy equivalence with the free-living isomorphism I serving as the interval: that is, if there exist maps g : B -> A and homotopies witnessing that gf and fg are homotopic to the identities.
children.closed_by: its own proof (content.tex:460-466), which constructs the inverse g and the homotopies by evaluating the induced equivalence on functor spaces and internalising via the cotensor universal property; the converse is immediate
children.note: Blueprint lemma node; \uses{defn:cosmos, defn:coherent-isomorphism, defn:equivalence}. Carries the converse direction of the glue (line 894); its proof cites lem:qcat-htpy-cat-equiv and prop:coherent-iso, giving depth 2.

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem whose goal is to exhibit a structure with several named components (here the seven items of an infinity-cosmos: objects, functor spaces, isofibrations, terminal object + products, pullbacks/towers, cotensors, equivalences), where each nontrivial component is verified by its own named lemma, and the parent's proof is a survey that cites those lemmas for the hard steps.
applicability.use_when: the structure has a finite, known list of components and the hard verification of each is a self-contained statement that can be stated and proved independently of the others; the parent proof is then a thin glue that walks the components and cites one lemma per nontrivial component.
applicability.avoid_when: the components share a genuinely common sub-argument (factor it into a third shared lemma first, as the proof's footnote pairs trivial-fib-conical with brown-fact); the components are so trivial that inline verification is clearer than a named lemma; or the component lemmas are not reusable elsewhere and only re-state the parent's burden.

claims.claim: The shape is a measurement: a 57-line parent site (845-901) whose proof cites 3 direct lemmas delegates the three nontrivial components to child proofs of 7 (421-427), 22 (546-567) and 16 (451-466) lines, and the longest chain of project lemmas below the proposition has depth 2 (lem:equiv-htpy-equiv cites lem:qcat-htpy-cat-equiv at line 463, a lemma stated without a blueprint proof at 307-312).
claims.evidence: line counts at the pinned commit: parent 901-845+1 = 57; children 427-421+1 = 7, 567-546+1 = 22, 466-451+1 = 16; the citation at https://github.com/emilyriehl/infinity-cosmos/blob/89d7dc3ed861824535e540da489a46469dcc8e56/blueprint/src/content.tex#L463 and the leaf lemma at #L307-L312

claims.claim: lem:equiv-htpy-equiv, the converse-direction child, is reused as the equivalence/homotopy-equivalence bridge at seven other places in the same blueprint (lines 480, 486, 496, 541, 1048, 1063, 1067), so it is a reusable component rather than a one-off for the slice construction.

metrics.how_counted: parent site = 845-901 (57 lines); the proof body = 881-901 (21 lines); children = 421-427 (7), 546-567 (22), 451-466 (16) = 45 lines, at the pinned commit

consequences: The parent proof walks the seven items of the cosmos structure and delegates the hard verifications to named lemmas, so the parent is a survey; a missing lemma, or a lemma whose statement does not cover the exact construction used in the slice, leaves a silent gap in the parent. The blueprint's \uses{} clause (line 882) names only two of the three lemmas (trivial-fib-conical and brown-fact); equiv-htpy-equiv is cited inline at line 894 but absent from the \uses{} list, so a reader following the \uses{} dependency graph alone misses the converse direction. Two of the three children (trivial-fib-conical and brown-fact) are paired for the pullback-stability footnote, so neither alone suffices for that step. The children are independent (none cites a sibling) but equiv-htpy-equiv is the single shared bridge reused throughout the chapter, so a defect in it breaks every later argument that routes through it.
